page: Alibaba Cloud ecs.u2a-c1m4.12xlarge is an x86_64 general-purpose instance powered by the KVM hypervisor. The system is equipped with 48 dedicated AMD EPYC vCPUs operating at a base frequency of 2.25 GHz, paired with 192.0 GB of system memory. This configuration maintains a standard 1:4 compute-to-memory ratio of 4.0 GB RAM per virtual core, providing stable, non-burstable processor resources for steady-state workloads.

The instance does not include bundled local storage, operating without attached ephemeral disks and relying entirely on external cloud storage volumes for file systems and data persistence. Network connectivity is configured with a baseline bandwidth of 13 Gbps. The instance provides zero complimentary public IPv4 addresses and does not include hardware acceleration, featuring a GPU count of zero.

Given its balanced ratio of 48 dedicated cores and 192 GB memory, ecs.u2a-c1m4.12xlarge delivers predictable capacity without the overhead of specialized hardware accelerators or local disk tiers. It is structured for workloads such as medium-to-large relational databases, distributed enterprise applications, container orchestration nodes, backend web serving fleets, and standard multi-threaded batch processing pipelines.
description: Alibaba Cloud ecs.u2a-c1m4.12xlarge is a general-purpose cloud server built on the KVM hypervisor and AMD EPYC x86_64 processor architecture. It delivers 48 dedicated vCPUs operating at 2.25 GHz alongside 192.0 GB of memory, preserving a standard 1:4 processor-to-memory ratio with 4.0 GB per core. The instance includes no local storage or onboard GPUs, relying on networked block storage for persistent data operations, and provides a 13 Gbps baseline network bandwidth. Without integrated ephemeral storage or accelerator components, the hardware profile avoids specialized infrastructure overheads while maintaining dedicated CPU allocations. This configuration is aligned with enterprise backend services, distributed middleware, relational database servers, container worker hosts, and multi-threaded data processing workloads requiring reliable core density and balanced capacity.
